title: The curve every empire follows
note: Ibn Khaldun charted how group solidarity carries a dynasty to power and then lets it fall.

research.quotes: heroes.html#f-word-and-page: 'Ibn Khaldun, 1332 to 1406, Tunis to Cairo.' 'he withdrew to a castle in Algeria... His Muqaddimah, the Introduction, written in 1377.' 'Asabiyya, group feeling, the solidarity of people bound together, lets a hardy folk take power; comfort then dissolves that solidarity over the generations until a hungrier group replaces them.' 'a report that violates the nature of society should be doubted, whoever tells it.'
research.retell: A historian named Ibn Khaldun found that a united people takes power, gets comfortable, loses its unity and is replaced by a hungrier united people, and nations still rise and fall that way.

lines.text: Why every empire falls the same way

lines.sub: Ibn Khaldun, a historian, writes a book

lines.text: A united people rises and takes power
A hungrier, united people takes over
Before him, history was just stories
lines.sub: he made it a science with laws

lines.text: Nations still rise and fall his way

lines.sub: group feeling, the bond that holds people
